Friend, I've spent the last year watching MAGA make life harder for the people of NJ-09. But I'm not just standing on the sidelines. I'm doing everything I can to fight back. I'm fighting to lower costs. Families in our district are struggling with the price of groceries, gas, and child care, and I'm pushing back on every MAGA policy that makes it worse. I'm fighting to protect healthcare. MAGA cut Medicaid and let ACA tax credits lapse, so I'm working to reverse those cuts and make sure no one in NJ-09 has to choose between paying rent and seeing a doctor. I'm fighting for accountability. Whether it's disaster aid held hostage for political reasons or dark money groups trying to buy this seat, I believe people deserve a government that answers to them, not to the highest bidder. [**This is why I ran for Congress, and it's why I'm running for re-election. But I can't do this work without you in my corner. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | Jacob Davis's Market Brief (ads) | • | Awesomely ---|--- • | Safe Money Report • | Weiss Ratings | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. subject: Maine families are being priced out of homeownership
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Bennett for Governor · P
body:
I have a real plan to make housing affordable. Help us take it statewide.

| | |
---
---
---
---
Peter For too many Maine families, the dream of owning a home is slipping further out of reach. Young families are doing everything right and still can’t get ahead. Workers can’t find homes near their jobs. Older Mainers are being squeezed by rising costs. And too many communities are struggling because housing has become too scarce and too expensive. **Maine needs real housing solutions** , not more delays, excuses, and politics as usual. That’s why I’ve put forward a plan to make housing affordable by:
* Helping first-time homebuyers with down payments
* Making monthly mortgage payments more manageable

Colorado Taxpayers Face Billion-Dollar TABOR Refund Money Grab Under Proposition NN
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/sbof5faa47e)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/s1i2baeb285)**
| | Hey friends,

**🎥 Freedom Festival Speaker Series Is Here!**

Missed a session at the Rocky Mountain Voice Freedom Festival? Or want to watch your favorite speaker again?

This week, we're releasing full speaker presentations from the festival on our YouTube channel. So far, you can watch [Mark Cook](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/s4p7bc6cade), [Dr. Kevin Roberts](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/s4n3f56c979), and [Lara Logan](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/s7ke747f340), with Beverly Vance Aikins and Kelsey Reinhardt of CatholicVote coming later today.

Whether you attended or couldn't make it, this is your chance to experience the conversations that made this year's festival so memorable. Be sure to [subscribe to our YouTube channel](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/scqbbcc6e47)—we'll be adding more full speeches throughout the week.
---
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/serdf62ad1d)
Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** Denver's DNC 2028 bid faces [hurdles from the state's deep-blue reputation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/s6n7d16c44a), while a teachers' union-backed coalition launched Proposition NN to [redirect over $1 billion in TABOR refunds to education](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/s8ibf4ec562), costing taxpayers about $7,300 each over a decade. Colorado's [new semiautomatic weapons law](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/sdubf4c7ca1) takes effect Aug. 1, air regulators advanced [gas-powered lawn equipment restrictions](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/sdo996db5bf), and the wildlife commission set [first-ever trapping limits](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/s2oa1046649) while rejecting a fur sales ban.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** VP JD Vance and Usha Vance welcomed their fourth child, Alec Neel Vance, the [first newborn to a sitting VP in over 150 years](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/s8g07a9f258). Trump's election security address drew [sharp reactions from Colorado lawmakers](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/scpd5bab284) after he released documents alleging Chinese interference in 2020 and called for securing the system ahead of the midterms.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Pastor Drake Hunter reflects on hide-and-seek and "olly, olly, oxen free" to explore Matthew 6's teaching on trust, arguing adults hide behind careers and success much as kids once hid behind trees, and that [faith means trusting God enough to stop hiding](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/sbh3e15389f).
This is your Mountain Minute for Tuesday, July 21, 2026.
– Team RMV
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Colorado Taxpayers Face Billion-Dollar TABOR Refund Money Grab Under Proposition NN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/s5s2b1777c8)** [COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/scheea73773)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/s8q87f9b21d)
A coalition that includes the state teachers’ union on Tuesday launched a campaign for a ballot proposal that would reduce more than $1 billion in taxpayer refunds and spend the money on education.
The measure is among several campaigns taking shape this year over state revenue. Broadly speaking, one side has long sought to raise more money, arguing what the state collects is insufficient to pay for services and programs. The other side counters that current revenues are sufficient but used unwisely, and what policymakers need is fiscal discipline.
Referred to the ballot by the state legislature via Senate Bill 135, the average Colorado taxpayer would lose about $7,300 in TABOR refunds between the 2026-27 and 2036-37 fiscal years if the proposal is approved at the ballot box, according to anonpartisan analysis.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/s4uf09c406b)**
|
---
**[Colorado Air Commission Advances Gas-Powered Lawn Equipment Restrictions](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/sdla91c8f80)** [THE SUM & SUBSTANCE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/s9i30fdc574)
_The AQCC scheduled a November rulemaking that would mandate a 90% reduction in commercial gas-powered lawn equipment over six years — targeting small landscaping businesses while exempting golf clubs and apartment complexes._
* The proposed rules cap commercial operators' gas-powered equipment at 90% in 2027, ratcheting down to just 10% by 2032 — covering push mowers, blowers, trimmers, edgers, and pruners, but exempting riding mowers and in-house groundskeepers at private entities.
* The same regulators rejected these restrictions in 2023 over job loss and cost concerns — and are now moving forward despite companies flagging real problems with electric alternatives including longer work times, battery fire risks, and costly recharging.
* The rule creates an uneven playing field: independent landscaping companies face mandatory compliance while golf clubs, apartment complexes, and other private entities with in-house staff are exempt — an attempt to expand the rule to cover those operators failed on a 4-3 commission vote.

**[The Hidden Trust Weapon: Olly, Olly, Oxen Free!](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/sek0f52c7d4)**
**BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | JULY 19** _“Olly, olly, oxen free!” If you’re smiling right now, you’re probably remembering the same thing I am. Long before smartphones, video games, and streaming television, neighborhood kids had an amazing ability to entertain themselves. We’d ride our bikes until the streetlights came on, play baseball in empty lots, build forts out of scrap lumber, and, when the evening shadows grew just a little longer, someone would shout, “Let’s play hide-and-seek!”_ __
**[Xcel says it has no affordability crisis. Its customers and regulatory filings tell another story.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/s4h82da41f2)**
**BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | JULY 17** _Every week, Carlos H. sits down with his bills and works out what his family can go without. Some weeks it is dinner. “I just opt out to say, hey, okay, maybe won’t be cooking up something tonight, so we can just make ends meet,” the Denver father said. Some weeks it is gas—a quarter tank instead of a full one, and the math of whether that gets him to the next payday._ __
**[The rise of DSA, and a platform to rewrite the Constitution.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/s8t380ea2ff)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._CQg/s7m39a15424)****BY SHAINA COLE | NATIONAL | JULY 16**
_Six thousand people started the Democratic Socialists of America in 1982. The number didn’t move much for thirty years. Then, around 2016, it did. By July 4, 2026, DSA had 120,000 members, more than the Socialist Party of America ever had under Eugene Debs, whose dues-paying membership peaked back in 1912._ __

body:
A discharge petition could force a vote on the Dream & Promise Act. Here's how we make Congress feel it. | | | Peter, For too long, our communities have been forced to live in fear and uncertainty. Entire workforces and families are being destabilized as millions of people are pushed out of status and out of work. And every time a family is separated, or a DACA recipient is detained without due process, Congress responds with statements and moments of silence instead of using the power it already has to stop the harm. **That ends now.** A discharge petition is moving through the House to force a vote on the Dream & Promise Act, a bill that would ensure citizenship for DACA recipients, immigrant youth, TPS holders, and those with Deferred Enforced Departure (DED). clean_body: A discharge petition could force a vote on the Dream & Promise Act. Here's how we make Congress feel it. | | | Peter, For too long, our communities have been forced to live in fear and uncertainty. Entire workforces and families are being destabilized as millions of people are pushed out of status and out of work. And every time a family is separated, or a DACA recipient is detained without due process, Congress responds with statements and moments of silence instead of using the power it already has to stop the harm. That ends now. A discharge petition is moving through the House to force a vote on the Dream & Promise Act, a bill that would ensure citizenship for DACA recipients, immigrant youth, TPS holders, and those with Deferred Enforced Departure (DED). This discharge petition is a chance for Congress to finally show up for everyday working people: the millions who work, pay taxes, raise families, and keep this country running. No more waiting. No more hiding behind process. We need 218 Members of Congress in the House to sign the discharge petition now. Our message is clear: citizenship is the only solution to the chaos, instability, and violence mass delegalization and immigration enforcement is creating — for working families, for employers, for local economies, for all of us. From the nurses caring for patients in rural hospitals, to the teachers in our children's schools, to the small business owners powering local economies — immigrants deliver for America every single day. Programs like DACA and TPS might be temporary, but the careers, families, and lives built over decades are not. It's time for Congress to decide: Will they stand with all workers who power America forward or with political dysfunction, chaos, and delay? | | | Friend, A child who survived the earthquake in Venezuela may have lost everything else.Their parents. Their home. Every relative who might have taken them in. Now they have nowhere to sleep, nothing to eat, and no one left to protect them.**When a child has nowhere to turn, someone else will offer to take her somewhere.** **Too often, that someone is a trafficker, and they know exactly how to make the offer sound like help. **
---
[](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=2e4cdfcdf6ea4ebf8f0c26628da9f8ca&_e=C4S8go7S7h-zIlpi811chO-negkWaaX9R9d_m43Fy5EEzGDMBVcdo05xb6v1GhSzM9NPVYAQ4rBv_yKBhgGvRJkD7G82K_dky6IKI9nF1C5jpwGqMOZLIEKgdYnfdaxDUepngoOS3c1Yhkc8pk603a_MbA58paw-doVJ2fot13yMyFIYNSAZ7kMbz7cCEJz6Xca4mOsAmuHFfKMHKy9DyE12XYrMvP9xP0avVbinYl7FPy2mDWUnragXez4YdayQuZFy8MVO_VkjLED-ru7ysFUvhmgp9vUeo_tnMeTOXFSPK9RGGnvntFDr5l3dX8ZmmOskiS4DzzNSPii308Yzd1ADTQNEuFYjlEy5QJJgjZBQf4NKVWqkivTsgHKTsUMj0mjL3pzVppJdhTX-ALr722yjs7Ct2XneBXzOJ5EXMa2pab4jSVUwTz9vT_i0azMm6W2YGuA8eF40ZjmVyqnRoxXAp_eD1JWsjeFT-NXQGHhVYGQ6GqE9iKiXoZUglrb1o0Vf9nvhKATT5pMFyN6f8QcF_KUcbdp3vnA3xil67QsZWtuh8Vp4E_l3aYY5O4lU3RIla2PId1BfQfzmTfBJiRc-wf-9V90DqEXAMpIceYkRmpU5eOLSf5_IEMxcFL6meGINIWOcVpHQzzK1kgPww1z3VWuhkQ8LAE8JrWkN4Z4NEvpqkwN95uLNdKiKGV81)

They study the gaps left behind by disaster, and they move quickly, often faster than the systems built to protect children can respond. A shelter without enough staff. A registration process that hasn't caught up. A crowd of frightened families too overwhelmed to watch every child closely. These are the openings traffickers are trained to find.

I produced the film Sound of Freedom, and founded the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** because I believe, without reservation, that every child deserves to be safe, and **none of them are for sale.** Right now, we are working urgently with organizations on the ground in Venezuela. We are helping so that displaced children what they need most: food, water, and a safe place to be found before a trafficker finds them first.

[](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=2e4cdfcdf6ea4ebf8f0c26628da9f8ca&_e=C4S8go7S7h-zIlpi811chO-negkWaaX9R9d_m43Fy5EEzGDMBVcdo05xb6v1GhSzM9NPVYAQ4rBv_yKBhgGvRJkD7G82K_dky6IKI9nF1C5jpwGqMOZLIEKgdYnfdaxDUepngoOS3c1Yhkc8pk603a_MbA58paw-doVJ2fot13yMyFIYNSAZ7kMbz7cCEJz6Xca4mOsAmuHFfKMHKy9DyE12XYrMvP9xP0avVbinYl7FPy2mDWUnragXez4YdayQOflwsEzgHaOfHdN4241aRoWG3oH75HR6JJIpqhukO57GJXwFaWAYVXfsJmh-Tbscos8jx37zux5vZBTAJu52un-ri1c36R4T6W4uLvSzH0dV0sTG82w4XB9EQNEleqge3YTIfBtUhDT7L8uRXsqF0IerHPeVXgogwGbjUnSuyT2obaPJ7VlryHpwT3xpnfPwjAXulgDv_avOPV92oxXi5gXWqggw8kWeCThUyglSngTjDWNwgNsRvSEaUFNICGXK4mZQv7bUVldaIMmE7tuZIQFHmpk57UtWkboLlmfNf-qRpytgsNVtkWCKWB8k3cLyz6b_K4DtEzqrEEDPkdaudtAEyqjqcGLQbzTVrhgr4uarSr0uoK4EzKDPArA9AnMSHbnCkpsH5ZK8DKeBaMb9Een-vlAWNKwUH93xNqW1HSMLoar9qUs-0e6bMs1vzkjL)

Much of Al-Mansouri lies in ruins, with the Israeli-occupied village of Majdal Zoun just across the valley. Despite the destruction and continued Israeli attacks, around 100 residents have chosen to remain. Al Mansouri, Lebanon. July 16, 2026. Photo by Katrine Dige Houmøller.
AL-MANSOURI, Lebanon--The road into Al-Mansouri winds through a shattered landscape. A barber shop stands without walls, its broken mirror still clinging to the remaining structure. The village cemetery is scarred by craters. The mosque is still standing, though parts of its façade were ripped away by Israeli airstrikes.
Nevertheless, over the past month, signs of life have returned to Al-Mansouri, a village in the Sour (Tyre) district near the coastline in southern Lebanon. On Thursday, a handful of men sat on plastic chairs outside their homes, sipping small cups of coffee. Others swept dust from damaged shops. Men on scooters wove between the ruins.
The same cannot be said for the neighboring village of Majdal Zoun which lies perched on a hill overlooking Al-Mansouri just a few hundred meters away. The two villages are closely intertwined and even share areas of territory that overlap. Last month, Israeli ground troops invaded and occupied Majdal Zoun, where they have been systematically [destroying](https://substack.com/redirect/eab10595-dc95-43d4-badd-2cb5c8412ff0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) homes and civilian infrastructure. The remaining residents of Al-Mansouri now live in full view of the occupying Israeli forces and under constant threat. Al-Mansouri is attacked on a near daily basis from its sister village with Israeli airstrikes and stun grenades dropped from drones.
Last month, Israeli aircraft dropped leaflets over Al-Mansouri, declaring the area a "threatened zone," telling residents to "stay away" and warning that anyone who approached Israeli forces would "put themselves in danger." Despite the threats, around 100 people have chosen to remain in the village, according to Yousef Shehemy, the mayor of neighboring Majdal Zoun, who has been displaced from his home by the occupying Israeli forces.
"People here believe their souls belong to this land," Shehemy told Drop Site as he drove past a row of destroyed houses in Al-Mansouri. Shehemy was in the village when the leaflets fell from the sky. "They want to control people's lives from above with leaflets, drones, sound grenades--all of it to frighten civilians."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e3c9b451-01e8-43ff-a110-932117f99ef8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

On June 29, Israel detonated what it described as a 200-metre Hezbollah tunnel beneath Majdal Zoun, leaving behind a massive crater. The blast site is visible on the left side of the hill. Majdal Zoun, Lebanon. July 16, 2026. Photo by Katrine Dige Houmøller.
Like dozens of villages and towns in southern Lebanon, Al-Mansouri and Majdal Zoun are either occupied by Israeli forces and being systematically destroyed, or being attacked from the air on a routine basis despite a U.S.-brokered framework agreement signed in Washington by the governments of Lebanon and Israel on June 26. The reality on the ground in Lebanon stands in stark contrast to what is being billed as an ongoing diplomatic effort to bring about a lasting peace deal.
On Tuesday, Lebanese president Joseph Aoun met with U.S. President Donald Trump, wrapping up a four-day visit to Washington. It marked the first meeting between leaders of the two countries for almost 20 years. "I would like to thank President Trump, really, and his team for the historic visit and for the historic achievement that we did together by signing the framework with the ultimate objective of ending the state of hostility between Lebanon and Israel forever," Aoun said in the White House.
The signed framework agreement requires the Lebanese Armed Forces to disarm Hezbollah before Israel withdraws from parts of Lebanese territory it occupies. Hezbollah has rejected the deal, which has been criticized for extracting few guarantees from Israel and placing nearly all obligations on the Lebanese government. Meanwhile, Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, have repeatedly vowed to keep occupying forces long term in a "security zone" in southern Lebanon.
In Al-Mansouri, the threat of Israeli troops invading the village is ever present. On Friday, [videos](https://substack.com/redirect/4d263117-5675-40d8-b277-9cd37af49ecf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) circulating on social media appeared to show an Israeli military vehicle advancing toward the Lebanese Army checkpoint at the entrance to the village before withdrawing.
"Israel is unpredictable," Shehemy said. "You never know what comes next."
Shehemy has served as mayor of Majdal Zoun for the past year. He fled the hilltop village with most of its residents when the war between Israel and Hezbollah escalated again on March 2. Before the latest phase of the war, around 1,500 people lived in Majdal Zoun. Today, the village stands empty and largely in ruins. According to Shehemy, 90 percent of Majdal Zoun has been destroyed by the Israeli military.
Across Lebanon, over 1.2 million people were forced from their homes by the Israeli assault, with more than 700,000 people in Lebanon still displaced despite a so-called "ceasefire," [according](https://substack.com/redirect/6ce4eefc-e16e-4ad1-ade1-dfdbacc8e2ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the United Nations.
"Everything has been put on standby. The war has prevented us from dreaming," Shehemy said.
For many families from Majdal Zoun, displacement has brought another painful uncertainty: the fate of missing relatives. Residents call Shehemy daily, inquiring about loved ones who disappeared after the village came under Israeli control in June. Some were civilians. Others fought alongside Hezbollah.
"They need to know the fate of their children," Shehemy said. "If it turns out they are dead, they would accept it. But without answers, these families will never find peace." Those answers remained out of reach. With Israeli forces still controlling Majdal Zoun, many residents see little chance of returning home anytime soon.
On Monday, the State Department announced that operations in three Lebanese villages deemed part of the so-called "pilot zones" had begun. The zones are nominally designed to allow the Lebanese army to replace Israeli troops in occupied areas.
Two of the villages, Froun and Srifa, were not under Israeli military control in the first place. On Tuesday, the Lebanese army began deploying to the third village, Zawtar al-Gharbieh, after Israel withdrew. However, Israeli forces opened fire near Lebanese troops as they were deploying, according to a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/0fc5184b-6a20-4b62-b6d6-8a864a31fa95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the Lebanese Army which warned the incident would "hinder the implementation of deployment steps" in the pilot zones.
To many residents of southern Lebanon, the agreement is little more than words on paper.
"As long as they are still occupying our land, I don't see any benefit in the framework agreement," Shehemy said from a coffee shop in Sour (Tyre) as an Israeli surveillance drone buzzed overhead. "They should make Israel withdraw from the occupied areas, not from zones that aren't even occupied."
He argued that the U.S. brokered negotiations have largely ignored the concerns of civilians who remain displaced. "For now, the negotiations are only one-sided, with Lebanon being used as a puppet by Israel."
Amnesty International has also criticized the framework agreement for appearing to "acquiesce to the prolonged and indefinite forced displacement of tens of thousands of residents of vast swathes of southern Lebanon occupied by Israeli forces." The deal violates international law, Amnesty said, as it "effectively consents to the prolonged and indefinite displacement of tens of thousands of residents of southern Lebanon by making their return, as well as reconstruction, contingent on conditions subject to 'confirmation.'"
Many residents in the south remain caught between distrust in the state and continued support for Hezbollah as a source of protection. Ali Ghandour, from Nabatieh in south Lebanon, spent months displaced in Saida after fleeing his home early in the war. At one point, he lived out of his car before eventually returning to his hometown. "What would you do if someone occupied your country and your president did nothing? You would fight back," he told Drop Site.
Ghandour said he feels abandoned by the Lebanese state, accusing the government of prioritizing U.S. and Israeli interests over its own citizens. "Only God protects us. And Hezbollah. As long as we have Hezbollah, we will be fine. When it comes to our country, we will never give up," he said.

Rescue workers from the Nabatieh Ambulance Association overlook the Nabatieh district as Israel continues to carry out air and drone strikes and demolitions despite the framework agreement. Nabatieh, Lebanon. July 16, 2026. Photo by Katrine Dige Houmøller.
Standing at Al Najda Al Shaabiya Hospital located on a hilltop overlooking Nabatieh, Israeli airstrikes echoed across the area on Thursday. Explosions shook surrounding villages, and smoke rose above the area of Zawtar on the horizon.
Over the past several weeks, the Israeli military has routinely violated the "ceasefire," conducting regular airstrikes, shelling, house demolitions, and other military operations. Residents and paramedics in Nabatieh said these actions are an almost daily reality in their district.
At the hospital, Fadel Sheet, a freelance journalist reporting for the Nabatieh Ambulance Association, pointed toward a rising cloud of smoke from an Israeli airstrike on Nabatieh Al Fawqa. "We are used to it. What can we do?" Sheet said. Just weeks earlier, another strike in the same village killed four people. The victims included a school principal, her mother, and two domestic workers who had gone to inspect their house. The Israeli military [acknowledged](https://substack.com/redirect/92a7f35b-5884-4953-a352-f58b29a58dc6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the attack, describing the four as approaching a "security zone" and claiming the strike was carried out to "eliminate the threat" of the four civilians to its forces.
Since March 2, more than 4,300 people have been killed in Israeli attacks, according to Lebanon's health ministry, including over 250 children. Over 12,200 have been injured.
Mahmoud Maoussa, a paramedic at the hospital, took a drag from his cigarette and pointed toward the smoke rising in the distance. "They are supposed to withdraw, but does it look like they are?"

"As long as they are still occupying our land, I don't see any benefit in the framework agreement," Shehemy said from a coffee shop in Sour (Tyre) as an Israeli surveillance drone buzzed overhead. "They should make Israel withdraw from the occupied areas, not from zones that aren't even occupied." He argued that the U.S. brokered negotiations have largely ignored the concerns of civilians who remain displaced. "For now, the negotiations are only one-sided, with Lebanon being used as a puppet by Israel." Amnesty International has also criticized the framework agreement for appearing to "acquiesce to the prolonged and indefinite forced displacement of tens of thousands of residents of vast swathes of southern Lebanon occupied by Israeli forces." The deal violates international law, Amnesty said, as it "effectively consents to the prolonged and indefinite displacement of tens of thousands of residents of southern Lebanon by making their return, as well as reconstruction, contingent on conditions subject to 'confirmation.'" Many residents in the south remain caught between distrust in the state and continued support for Hezbollah as a source of protection. Ali Ghandour, from Nabatieh in south Lebanon, spent months displaced in Saida after fleeing his home early in the war. At one point, he lived out of his car before eventually returning to his hometown. "What would you do if someone occupied your country and your president did nothing? You would fight back," he told Drop Site. Ghandour said he feels abandoned by the Lebanese state, accusing the government of prioritizing U.S. and Israeli interests over its own citizens. "Only God protects us. And Hezbollah. As long as we have Hezbollah, we will be fine. When it comes to our country, we will never give up," he said. | | ---|---|--- Rescue workers from the Nabatieh Ambulance Association overlook the Nabatieh district as Israel continues to carry out air and drone strikes and demolitions despite the framework agreement. Nabatieh, Lebanon. July 16, 2026. Photo by Katrine Dige Houmøller. Standing at Al Najda Al Shaabiya Hospital located on a hilltop overlooking Nabatieh, Israeli airstrikes echoed across the area on Thursday. Explosions shook surrounding villages, and smoke rose above the area of Zawtar on the horizon. Over the past several weeks, the Israeli military has routinely violated the "ceasefire," conducting regular airstrikes, shelling, house demolitions, and other military operations. Residents and paramedics in Nabatieh said these actions are an almost daily reality in their district. At the hospital, Fadel Sheet, a freelance journalist reporting for the Nabatieh Ambulance Association, pointed toward a rising cloud of smoke from an Israeli airstrike on Nabatieh Al Fawqa. "We are used to it. What can we do?" Sheet said. Just weeks earlier, another strike in the same village killed four people. The victims included a school principal, her mother, and two domestic workers who had gone to inspect their house. The Israeli military the attack, describing the four as approaching a "security zone" and claiming the strike was carried out to "eliminate the threat" of the four civilians to its forces. Since March 2, more than 4,300 people have been killed in Israeli attacks, according to Lebanon's health ministry, including over 250 children. Over 12,200 have been injured. Mahmoud Maoussa, a paramedic at the hospital, took a drag from his cigarette and pointed toward the smoke rising in the distance. "They are supposed to withdraw, but does it look like they are?" | A guest post by| journalist working in the Middle East for four years, covering war and humanitarian crises through written journalism, photography and live broadcasting. Republicans aren't slowing down.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135720495/635123715/297443936?refcode=BLU_EM_SSFC_2026-07-21_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTgxNzYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTljM2I2ZjUtMzg4NS1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=gzjOyPNSdVu6D64D87MuDCmOIPPJwEoabDOBaofy1WQ=) PPeter,

We're more than halfway through July, and **we're not even halfway to our $150,000 fundraising goal**.

That's a big problem.

Republicans aren't slowing down. MAGA groups are spending. Billionaire donors are writing checks. Our opponent already has TV ads on the air, and even more outside money is on the way because they know NH-01 could decide control of the House.

Derek, I know my

But there’s a good explanation for why we have to reach out so often.

In a state as competitive as Pennsylvania, campaigns like ours can’t win
without a steady stream of grassroots support. Sure, a ton of our budget
will be spent in October — the final weeks before Election Day.

But throughout those final weeks, we’ll be spending more than we’re
bringing in. That’s the only way we’ll be able to win.

That’s why the war chest we’re able to build today truly
matters, Derek.
Every dollar we bring in doesn’t only fund our events and outreach efforts
today. It funds our TV ads in October, our GOTV efforts in November, and
everything else we need to win this race on November 3rd.

To put it another way: There’s no better time to make a contribution to
our campaign than right now.

I've gotten to know a lot of folks in public service, and I can't think of many who've done more to live out our values than Jim Clyburn.

Jim has always believed America's greatness ought to be accessible and affordable to everybody, not just some. He spent much of his life proving that, first as a leading figure in the Civil Rights Movement, blazing a path for justice and equality that so many of us are still walking today.

As House Majority Whip and Assistant Democratic Leader, Jim became one of the most effective advocates this country has ever had for voting rights, affordable health care, broadband expansion, and civil rights. That's not small stuff. That's the kind of work that changes people's lives.

And he hasn't slowed down. Jim's still out there fighting to protect our communities from what this administration keeps throwing at them, showing the rest of us how to push back the right way, and traveling the country to help elect good Democrats up and down the ballot.

I want to wish the Congressman a happy birthday and say thank you for everything he's done for this country. And I think the best way we can actually thank him is by helping Democrats win this November and beyond.

Fellow Conservative,

I do not usually write at length, but this is worth a few extra minutes of your time.

People look at South Dakota, a good and conservative state, and assume my seat is safe. I understand why. But that assumption is precisely the vulnerability the other side is counting on. They are not trying to win here by convincing South Dakotans to become Democrats, because they know that will never work. Instead, they are trying to win by disguise, running a man who was their own nominee just two years ago under the banner of an "independent," and hoping just enough good people let their guard down.

And the prize, if they pull it off, is enormous. **A single seat is the difference between a Senate that confirms constitutional judges and one that lets Chuck Schumer pack the courts.** It is the difference between an America First agenda that keeps moving and one that dies in committee. The whole direction of the country can turn on a race exactly like this one.

That is why I refuse to coast, and why I am asking for your help in the middle of a quiet July instead of waiting for a loud October.

clean_body: A single seat is the difference between a Senate that confirms constitutional judges and one that lets Chuck Schumer pack the courts. | Fellow Conservative, I do not usually write at length, but this is worth a few extra minutes of your time. People look at South Dakota, a good and conservative state, and assume my seat is safe. I understand why. But that assumption is precisely the vulnerability the other side is counting on. They are not trying to win here by convincing South Dakotans to become Democrats, because they know that will never work. Instead, they are trying to win by disguise, running a man who was their own nominee just two years ago under the banner of an "independent," and hoping just enough good people let their guard down. And the prize, if they pull it off, is enormous. A single seat is the difference between a Senate that confirms constitutional judges and one that lets Chuck Schumer pack the courts. It is the difference between an America First agenda that keeps moving and one that dies in committee. The whole direction of the country can turn on a race exactly like this one. That is why I refuse to coast, and why I am asking for your help in the middle of a quiet July instead of waiting for a loud October. Thank you for reading all of that. It tells me you take this as seriously as I do. Gratefully, Mike Rounds FOLLOW MIKE ON SOCIAL MEDIA: | | Paid for by Rounds for Senate Don't want to receive any more of our emails? [ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

This week, the House is RACING to push through its must-pass National
Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), which not only would send $1.15 TRILLION
to the Pentagon, but includes a section that would HARDWIRE U.S. military
support to Israel, tying the U.S. even more tightly to the Netanyahu
government.

Last week, Democrats in the Senate blocked debate on the NDAA because of
Trump’s war on Iran. But our work is nowhere near done. Now it’s the
House’s turn, and the vote will happen THIS WEEK before the House goes on
recess.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39201?source=email-20260721&t=1011&akid=11081%2E5885482%2Ex62d77 ]Headline: Senate Stalls NDAA With Major Israel Plan Critics Call
‘Treason’

Negotiations are happening right now, and the only way to stop this is if
thousands of us speak out immediately and demand that Congress stop
Section 219 from becoming law.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39201?source=email-20260721&t=1012&akid=11081%2E5885482%2Ex62d77 ]Add your name now: Tell Congress to strip Section 219 from the NDAA
before it’s too late!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39201?source=email-20260721&t=1013&akid=11081%2E5885482%2Ex62d77 ]ADD YOUR NAME

Section 219 was written by lobbyists and Netanyahu himself. The merger
would supersize weapons deals, surveillance tech, and intelligence sharing
for years to come, no matter what voters might want. It would strip away
even the limited Congressional checks that exist today, making the
U.S.-Israel military partnership more secretive, less accountable, and
even harder for the public – or even Congress itself – to monitor.

This outrageous plan comes as the tide is turning in DC. Last week, a
MAJORITY of House Democrats (103 in total!) voted to strip $3.3 BILLION in
military funding to Israel.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39201?source=email-20260721&t=1014&akid=11081%2E5885482%2Ex62d77 ]Headline: A House vote makes it clear: Israel’s support among Democrats
is starting to buckle

The truth is that a growing majority of Americans oppose unconditional
support for the Israeli government in the midst of mass violence. That’s
why a bipartisan group of leaders tried to stop the proposed US/Israel
military merger with an amendment. Then, the House Rules Committee shut it
down, preventing a full vote.

Let’s be clear: not one dime of our money should go to enable Israel’s
collective punishment, targeting of civilians, or expansion of illegal
settlements. Congress must not entangle us deeper in endless war.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39201?source=email-20260721&t=1015&akid=11081%2E5885482%2Ex62d77 ]Take action now. Add your name to send a loud, unified message: No more
blank checks for endless wars, no secret deals, and no more complicity in

When we organize, we win.

| | **_Meet Rob:_** Born and raised in Kingston, PA, Rob Bresnahan is currently serving his first term as PA-08’s homegrown Congressman. He’s a fifth-generation Northeastern Pennsylvanian, and the only representative in Congress who is part of the National Electrical Contractors Association. A product of the American Dream, Rob learned the true meaning of hard work by getting his hands dirty early and often. He wired junction boxes, ran heavy equipment, drove trucks, and learned the value of an honest day’s work in the process. His family instilled the values of hard work, discipline, and perseverance in him at a young age – and Rob has stayed true to these foundational values all his life. At just 19 years old, Rob joined his family’s business as the CFO for Kuharchik Construction. He became the CEO of the company in 2013. Rob spent over a decade working and connecting with blue-collar Americans across the country before running for Congress in 2024. He was outspent 2:1 in his race against a 12-year Democrat that year, but the people of Northeastern Pennsylvania demanded change when they sent Rob to be their fighter in Washington. Through his experience as an electrical contractor, Rob saw the real world struggles facing America’s blue-collar workers first hand. Wages are not keeping up with the skyrocketing cost of living, and Americans who wake up every day and pay their dues are being left out to dry by their elected officials. But Rob’s voting record in Congress tells a different story. He’s stood up for hardworking Americans at every opportunity, regardless of partisan politics. Simply put, Rob Bresnahan brings both insight and candid concern for blue-collar America to Congress that your run-of-the-mill representatives don’t. Every day that he steps foot on Capitol Hill, Rob is 100% devoted to restoring America’s energy independence, deregulating the economy, and bringing well-paying jobs back to the great commonwealth of Pennsylvania. While he’s still serving his freshman term in Congress, Rob has already introduced key legislation to re-invest in American trades and pave avenues to success for young people who forgo a traditional college education. Now running for re-election in one of the most pivotal battleground races in the country, Rob is stepping up to the plate once again to deliver for the people of PA-08 and preserve our Republican House majority for the remainder of President Trump’s second term.

body:
https://drshirleyweber.com/?utm_source=email%20wrapper&utm_medium=email%20wrapper&utm_campaign=email%20wrapper [https://drshirleyweber.com/?utm_source=email%20wrapper&utm_medium=email%20wrapper&utm_campaign=email%20wrapper]
Dear friends,

On July 10 my office certified the results of California’s June 2 Primary Election. 9,446,461 Californians cast a ballot – 40.8% of registered voters, up from 33.2% in 2022.

While we knew the outcome of most races within a few days of the election, it took six weeks to fully account for and document every vote. You may have heard certain politicians attacking our elections because of this pace – but I want to explain why those attacks are misguided.

In California, we care far more about getting the count right than getting it done quickly. And we’ve designed our elections to make sure as many people as possible are able to exercise their sacred right to vote.

Those two commitments – accuracy and accessibility – are why our count takes the time that it does.

In California, we mail a ballot to every registered California voter, and count those ballots so long as they are correctly filled out and put in the mail by election day. To give you an idea of what that commitment looks like in practice, here is what actually happens during the weeks after election day:

More than 8.4 million of this primary’s ballots were returned by mail. Each one of those ballots is verified before it is opened: the signature on the envelope is compared against the signatures in that voter’s registration file.

When something doesn’t match – and signatures do change, with age, with injury, and over time – the ballot isn’t discarded. The county contacts the voter, and the voter has time to confirm that the ballot is theirs.

This year, thousands of Californians “cured” their ballots using that exact process. That step takes weeks, and it is supposed to – because it guarantees that valid votes are not thrown out.

Then, before anything is certified, each county audits their results. We check our work, and make sure that everything adds up. Once we’re certain of the results, we publish a full Statement of the Vote – a transparent accounting of every contest, every vote cast, and every total – that can be reviewed and examined by everyone.

You can read the full Statement of the Vote for the June 2 Primary Election here. [https://elections.cdn.sos.ca.gov/sov/2026-primary/sov/complete-sov.pdf] Read now » [https://elections.cdn.sos.ca.gov/sov/2026-primary/sov/complete-sov.pdf] Ordinarily, this is where I would sign off. But this past week, the President dedicated a primetime address to repeating thoroughly debunked claims about American elections – and the following morning, the Secretary of Homeland Security alleged that California has nearly 200,000 “noncitizens” registered to vote.

If the President’s address is anything to go off of, I have some doubts about the methodology used to arrive at these conclusions.

To date, the Trump Administration has not yet explained how it produced that number, what records it relied on, or whether anyone on its list is actually a noncitizen – much less whether anyone actually voted when they shouldn’t have.

If the Federal Government is truly interested in upholding our democracy, they must stop undermining confidence in our elections.

Under the Constitution, state and local governments run elections. Not Donald Trump, Markwayne Mullin, or anyone else in the Trump Administration.

Every time they ignore that fact, they disrespect the underpinnings of our democracy, the people who work tirelessly to keep our elections safe, and the generations of Americans who fought to defend our right to the ballot box.

So that is the story of the past seven weeks. No mystery, no mistake – just America’s biggest state collecting and counting millions of ballots, with thousands of election workers working overtime to make sure every single one of those votes was counted properly.

I am grateful to them, and to every Californian who participated in our June Primary.

I do not take my position as Secretary of State for granted, and I will always use my office to uphold the values and laws that underpin our democracy.

Onward,

Dr. Shirley N Weber

P.S. If you’d like to see California count ballots more quickly while upholding our values of accessibility and accuracy, you can call your representatives in the State Legislature and ask them to provide more funding to county election administrators.

I spent twenty one years in the Navy, and I can tell you that in a ready room, "we don't have the resources" buys you about four seconds of sympathy. Somebody asks what you've actually got, you start listing it out loud, and the excuse usually dies right there. Nine times out of ten the resources are there. They're just aimed at the wrong things, at the wrong tempo, out of habit instead of judgment.
Thanks for reading Jason Knapp! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..Vugz3tnMIwPnEHUrE_CEVCTlPf_s4Vl4zIdhQLGYlIs?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=207821372)
### House Democrats have the resources.
Yes, we're in the minority, and I'm not going to pretend that doesn't matter. The Speaker controls the floor, committee chairs control the gavels, the majority controls the subpoenas, and none of that changes before January 2027. But look what happened the moment the minority stopped waiting for permission. A discharge petition forced the Epstein files into the open. Another one restored collective bargaining rights for federal workers. A third pushed an ACA extension to the floor over the Speaker's objection. So the tools work. What we don't have yet is the machine that runs those tools every single day, in every office, at scale. And the country is paying for that gap.
Let me also be clear about what this piece is not. It's not a pile-on against Hakeem Jeffries. He's not the Speaker and he doesn't have the Speaker's tools. Frankly, most of the people going after him are just looking for a target. My argument is about the playbook. I want to help build the machine that runs it.
### What's actually happening
Democrats are fighting, and winning more than the doom loop admits. Oversight Democrats subpoenaed the Justice Department from the minority, which almost never happens. State attorneys general have won injunction after injunction. That work is real and I don't want to talk past it.
But too much of the daily response still runs on the same three plays: sharp committee moments cut for social media, fundraising emails written around whatever the day's outrage is, and floor speeches delivered to an empty chamber. Each of those has a place. None of them is close to sufficient against what we're up against.
Meanwhile the institutional capacity to investigate this administration has been gutted, and I mean that literally, not as a figure of speech. The House Appropriations Committee's Surveys and Investigations staff, the people who used to do confidential, bipartisan, fact-driven oversight, was disbanded in December 2024. More than 20 inspectors general have been fired or forced out since January 2025. Last fall the White House cut off funding for the Council of the Inspectors General, which supports all 72 watchdog offices. Oversight.gov and more than fifteen inspector general websites went dark, taking 34,000 public reports with them. The money only came back after Republican senators pushed, and even now the administration's own budget proposes cutting inspector general funding by nearly a quarter.
And if you step back further the picture gets worse. The Government Accountability Office has lost roughly 44 percent of its workforce since the late 1970s. The Congressional Research Service is down 28 percent. House committee staff fell from 2,027 people in 1979 to 1,272 by 2005 and never recovered.
None of this happened by accident. Somebody benefits when Congress is too thin to do its job. Corporate lobbyists benefit. Contractors benefit. The donors writing the big checks benefit. The people who eat the costs are you.
So the real question is bigger than how we fight this administration. It's this: with what's left of the institution, what can we build, and what's the playbook for using every tool we've got?
Because the tools do exist. Discharge petitions that can force any bill to the floor with 218 signatures. Privileged resolutions that move on a fixed clock the majority can't ignore. GAO studies, inspector general referrals, and FOIA requests that any member can file, minority or not. Shadow hearings any committee can hold outside the majority's control. Coalition partners with real power, meaning state attorneys general with subpoenas, governors who actually run agencies, and Senate offices holding filibuster leverage on must-pass bills. Plus the votes Republicans cannot get without us on the NDAA, on appropriations, on the debt ceiling.
On paper that's a lot. In practice almost none of it is being run at scale, and that's the part I can't accept.
### Seven things every Democratic House office could be doing right now
I want to be specific here, because abstractions are how we got into this mess.
**1\. Run discharge petitions as public campaigns, not parliamentary maneuvers.** This is the play that's already working. The Epstein files, the collective bargaining restoration, the ACA extension. Every one of them started as a petition people said would fail. So, let's keep the pipeline full. You don't need 218 signatures on day one, you need 200 reliable Democratic signatures and a target list of the most vulnerable Republicans. Pick the next bills where the public is already with us: things like drug pricing, an ethics package, voting rights. Let's build a public scoreboard. Run paid media in each holdout district until the pressure gets uncomfortable. The petition itself is the message, and the vote, if we get one, is the bonus.
**2\. Treat shadow hearings like a documentary series instead of a press conference.** Democrats have started down this road. This year's shadow hearings have drawn millions of views online, and Oversight Democrats took survivor testimony on the road. What's missing now is discipline. Do it monthly, brand it, and give each episode one topic: a fired inspector general, a contract handed to a donor, a defunded program with named victims. Put real production values behind it and distribute it. The January 6 Select Committee showed what the standard looks like. Meet that every single month in a sustained way.
**3\. Build a permanent GAO, inspector general, and FOIA operation.** The Rapid Response Task Force is the right instinct and its briefs are already getting cited in federal court rulings. But a working group of members is not an institution. What is missing is a single minority-side records operation with professional staff and a sustained budget: one intake portal, quarterly public reports, oversight run the way the Heritage Foundation runs policy. That still does not exist anywhere in the House, and it should outlast any one Congress.
**4\. Build a three-channel pipeline.** Every record that operation produces should feed three places at once: a state attorney general who can act on it, a Senate office that can hold a hearing on it, and a member whose own constituents are affected by it. The pipeline is what turns one document into three fights.
**5\. Hold field hearings where people are actually being hurt.** Not in Washington. Go to the rural counties that lost their hospitals. Go to the federal worker neighborhoods of Northern Virginia. Come to the Northern Neck, where our watermen are losing their grounds. Bring witnesses and bring cameras, then carry the record back to Washington as evidence.
**6\. Run constituent service as a public commitment, not a back-office function.** Every fired federal worker, every veteran whose claim got kicked back, every Medicaid recipient losing coverage should have one phone number to call, a trained staff on the other end, and a published record of cases resolved. Rick Boucher built exactly this in Southwest Virginia and people still talk about it. It should be standard in every Democratic district. The work is the message.
**7\. Hold ourselves to the Truman standard, not the dunking standard.** The Truman Committee saved an estimated $10 to $15 billion in wartime spending, along with thousands of American lives, and it worked because it stuck to the facts, treated witnesses with respect, and built bipartisan buy-in. Decades later, Carl Levin's Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations did the same thing, and Levin didn't stop at hearings. He handed cases to the Justice Department on a silver platter. That's the bar I want us measured against. We need cases, not YouTube clips.
I know this may read like a wish list. It isn't. **It 's work. **It takes staff time, sustained attention, and a willingness to invest in things that won't pay off in this week's news cycle. Which is why none of this happens by default. Someone has to build it, fund it, and staff it. That's the job I'm applying for.
For 18 months this administration has been firing watchdogs, cutting benefits, and dismantling the machinery of democracy. So here's the standard I think voters should hold every member of Congress to, in both parties, and it's the one I'm asking you to hold me to starting day one.
_How many discharge petitions carry your name? How many shadow hearings have you hosted in your district? How many GAO requests have you filed, how many inspector general referrals? And how many of your constituents who lost a federal job or a federal benefit were assisted by your office?_
These aren't gotcha questions. They're the job description. Plenty of members can answer them well right now. Some can't. The goal is a Congress where all of them can.
### What I will do
In my first 100 days, I'll sign every active discharge petition that has Democratic majority support. I'll introduce a resolution of inquiry on every fired inspector general whose case hasn't been formally accounted for. I'll hold a quarterly field hearing right here in this district, in Reedville, Gloucester, Williamsburg, Midlothian, with my own constituents as the witnesses, on the record. And I'll publish a public dashboard showing every constituent case my office takes on and how it ends, the wins _and_ the losses both. Accountability matters.
I'll also be honest about what I can't do alone. The minority needs an institutional response, not a hundred individual ones. Until somebody runs a coordinated playbook, every member should be running it themselves. That's the bare minimum this moment requires of us.
### The part that's on you
The American system was built on the assumption that people in office would treat the office as a trust. When they don't, and I'd argue we've reached that point, the system falls back on a second assumption: that voters will notice and act.
So look at the people representing you, in both parties. Ask what they've built in the last 18 months. Ask what tools they've used, what cases their offices have closed, what hearings they've held in the places they actually represent.
If the answers are good, keep them. Some of them have earned your vote.
If not, the Virginia's primary is August 4th and the general is in November.
And if you want to help build this kind of politics in VA-01, we're doing it right now, with volunteers knocking doors and banking early votes across all 18 localities. Join us.

|
Peter,
The last few weeks have been terrifying for Democracy.
Trump went on primetime to resurrect his election-fraud fantasy, laying the groundwork to contest any result he doesn't like. Stephen Miller stood at the State Department and called Americans on the left a "cancer" to be "rooted out." The FBI raided the Ohio Organizing Collaborative and opened an investigation into America Votes, two groups whose only crime is registering voters.
And this week, Trump's reign of terror continues. On Monday, the State Department published a report titled "Cuba: The Capital of 21st Century Communism." Buried inside it is something that has no business existing in a free country: a list of specific American citizens, named and targeted by their own government for their politics.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001oOzahmgTAetL9q1l_It9erl_2zmm7ofrOB4aSCZkyrGhJPuDDXpb13ke2zwOi5a_ltKuaY6zoDGF-FAN327GtQ_wsERYLeNFfdDK3FMuDyv3_5EhpS-pwWsCXb-IqnwFW9_UCD08j0QeBg2p9WIRcGsOUDafAw2d9fakBhjTzwudEOPyApPRU7V3MLQLaQUMEJTd5cNr_yWw1TesTbDbE_tEhE21go7ZPJkgjCl_5ng=&c=OiIF3wrYbasoGKV-ALu4oHCa-7FvdhJwwhLDhRZc3f_AtXaACqwaow==&ch=pOAsqHKY2PsLwmvPV8w29CdWpaOIMkEA8DoP-nEffVIe_eddbdClfQ==)
---
A pattern is starting to emerge.
The report singles out streamer Hasan Piker, Amazon union organizer Christian Smalls, the Democratic Socialists of America, and environmental activist Isra Hirsi, the daughter of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar. It brands them "front groups and fellow travelers" for a foreign government, and it reaches back to the McCarthy era for its playbook, holding up the blacklists and loyalty purges of the 1950s as a model that worked.
You don't have to agree with one word these people have ever said to see the danger. The instant the government starts printing lists of citizens to punish for their beliefs, the only question left is will my name get added next.
And just as terrifying, this report serves another insidious purpose: it lays the groundwork for regime change in Cuba as Trump continues to threaten an invasion. A witch hunt at home and another war abroad.
That's why Defend Our Courts' work is so critical at this moment. Trump's attempt at a fascist takeover of our country is exactly what our courts were built to stop. The judges we elect this November will play a decisive role in whether our democracy holds or not. We're fighting to expand and protect the Democratic firewall of state Supreme Courts nationwide--courts that have the power to stop Trump.
But to operate at the scale we need to at this pivotal moment requires resources we don't have yet. We need the support of Democrats everywhere to help fuel our efforts. clean_body: The instant the government starts printing lists of citizens to punish for their beliefs, the only question left is whose name will get added next. | | | | | == | Peter, The last few weeks have been terrifying for Democracy. Trump went on primetime to resurrect his election-fraud fantasy, laying the groundwork to contest any result he doesn't like. Stephen Miller stood at the State Department and called Americans on the left a "cancer" to be "rooted out." The FBI raided the Ohio Organizing Collaborative and opened an investigation into America Votes, two groups whose only crime is registering voters. And this week, Trump's reign of terror continues. On Monday, the State Department published a report titled "Cuba: The Capital of 21st Century Communism." Buried inside it is something that has no business existing in a free country: a list of specific American citizens, named and targeted by their own government for their politics. | == A pattern is starting to emerge. The report singles out streamer Hasan Piker, Amazon union organizer Christian Smalls, the Democratic Socialists of America, and environmental activist Isra Hirsi, the daughter of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar. It brands them "front groups and fellow travelers" for a foreign government, and it reaches back to the McCarthy era for its playbook, holding up the blacklists and loyalty purges of the 1950s as a model that worked. You don't have to agree with one word these people have ever said to see the danger. The instant the government starts printing lists of citizens to punish for their beliefs, the only question left is will my name get added next. And just as terrifying, this report serves another insidious purpose: it lays the groundwork for regime change in Cuba as Trump continues to threaten an invasion. A witch hunt at home and another war abroad. That's why Defend Our Courts' work is so critical at this moment. Trump's attempt at a fascist takeover of our country is exactly what our courts were built to stop. The judges we elect this November will play a decisive role in whether our democracy holds or not. We're fighting to expand and protect the Democratic firewall of state Supreme Courts nationwide--courts that have the power to stop Trump. But to operate at the scale we need to at this pivotal moment requires resources we don't have yet. We need the support of Democrats everywhere to help fuel our efforts. body:
Right now, the Trump administration is continuing to inflict cruelty upon immigrant communities across our country.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260721-6495-footer&t=1&akid=6495%2E420207%2E0oOi3p)
Peter,
As you read this email, the Trump administration is escalating its campaign of cruelty against immigrant communities.
Masked, unidentified ICE agents are still grabbing people off the streets. Still terrorizing families and neighborhoods. Innocent people are still dying as a result of these enforcement actions—with no accountability.
And now, they are ripping Temporary Protected Status away from people who’ve built their lives here for years, and who face real danger back in their home countries. They’ve paused asylum applications for people fleeing violence and persecution, and they’ve reinstated a ban on entry from several Muslim-majority countries.
**This is cruelty for cruelty’s sake, and it needs to end.**
I came to this country alone at 16 to go to school. I know what it feels like to be scared, far from home, and unsure what your future holds. And while I got the chance to live my American dream, this administration is currently slamming the door shut on millions of others.
That’s why I’m fighting so hard and standing up to ICE directly. I’ve sponsored and introduced key legislation in Congress, including:
* **Orlin’s Law** , named after a 3-year-old boy who was killed after being separated from his deported mother, which would prevent ICE from detaining or deporting primary caregiver parents unless they pose a specific public safety threat

* **The Dignity for Detained Immigrants Act** , which would end mandatory detention, prohibit the jailing of children, and phase out the use of private, for-profit detention centers

* **The PROTECT Immigration Act** , which would stop local police from being forced to act as federal immigration agents so that we can rebuild trust between immigrant communities and local law enforcement

* **The LIFT the BAR Act** , which would remove strict five-year waiting periods and allow green card holders, DACA recipients, and other lawfully present immigrants to access essential federal programs

But Peter, none of this will pass on its own. It’s going to take a movement willing to fight for it, and a more progressive Congress that’s willing to stand up for immigrant communities.
I’m working to elect progressives across the country this November, but I can’t do it without your support. I don’t take corporate PAC money, and I don’t have billionaires on speed dial to fund my campaign. Our movement is powered by grassroots supporters like you.
[**So Peter, if you’re with me in the fight for immigration justice, can I count on you to pitch in $3 or whatever you’re able today?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260721.8wx4CX&refcode=em20260721-6495&amount=3&t=2&akid=6495%2E420207%2E0oOi3p)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260721.8wx4CX&amount=3&refcode=em20260721-6495&t=21&akid=6495%2E420207%2E0oOi3p)**
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal
**[Contribute](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-footer?refcode=em20260721-6495-footer&t=22&refcode2=6495_420207_0oOi3p&akid=6495%2E420207%2E0oOi3p)**

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way we keep in touch with people like you, and small-dollar contributions sustain our movement for transformative change. To contribute by check, please address to Pramila for Congress, PO Box 21912, Seattle, WA 98111.

Power, Prosperity, Peace
| Dear Friends, New England is a close-knit region — news in one state ripples into the others. That's why I want to acknowledge the recent nurses' strike in Massachusetts: many Granite Staters rely on Mass General Brigham, whether for their jobs or their healthcare. This was the largest nurses' strike in Massachusetts history. The Massachusetts Nurses Association made clear[ this was the result](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/Fl97sWr691Meq1YkK3AHKUwMBCIVNNoV/click?signature=069c50a8c388ccbf8b0fc9e0f3a5b15ec096f5cb&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.massnurses.org%2F2026%2F07%2F08%2Fjuly-8-strike-of-4500-mna-nurses-clinicians-begins-wednesday-morning-after-mgb-billionaires-refuse-to-negotiate-fair-contracts-for-safe-patient-care%2F) of wealthy, powerful executives' refusal to negotiate in good faith or meet the needs of healthcare professionals. To make matters worse, the nurses ended their strike but[ were locked out of their job](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/Fl97sWr691Meq1YkK3AHKUwMBCIVNNoV/click?signature=d6cad1a9e5058ea785859d98d7fc0460cc3fd4c6&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cbsnews.com%2Fboston%2Fnews%2Fbrigham-and-womens-hospital-nurses-lockout-strike-boston%2F)s for several days. As a registered nurse, I understand that lives are at stake when healthcare professionals are denied the respect, security, and working conditions they need and deserve. I come from a working-class family. I am pro-union and pro-worker. I stand with the nurses of Mass General Brigham. The parallels between the strike and our movement are undeniable. Many of you are also nurses, healthcare professionals, working Americans, and working families. You might know someone who participated in this strike or maybe you participated yourself. **I KNOW many of you understand the struggle of working too hard and still not having enough to make ends meet.** What is happening at Mass General Brigham is happening to nearly every worker in America: wealthy employers are preventing their employees from the pay, benefits, and _the lives_ they have earned through their work. I am championing you, too. Your needs matter. Your families' needs matter. As an elected official, I will continue standing with you. I will fight for laws that will improve the lives of all of us.
* * *
**Let’s connect and talk about what your community needs!** I've got a jam-packed week ahead — here's where you can find me: **📅 Thursday, July 23rd**
I'll be in **Lebanon** at the [Farmers' Market](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/Fl97sWr691Meq1YkK3AHKUwMBCIVNNoV/click?signature=30927f96ac8a6c61f653b03d2c0ca50492e32e23&url=https%3A%2F%2Flebanonnh.gov%2F806%2FFarmers-Market) from **4–7 pm** — come say hi while I browse the veggies! Then I'm sticking around for the [Front Porch Concert series](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/Fl97sWr691Meq1YkK3AHKUwMBCIVNNoV/click?signature=2ad4b5febc2f17a083463f81eb1ea77b96b50fdb&url=https%3A%2F%2Flebanonnh.gov%2F367%2FFront-Porch-Concert-Series), **7–9 pm**. **📅 Friday, July 24th**
Fair day! I'll be soaking up all the fun in **Haverhill** at the [North Haverhill Fair](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/Fl97sWr691Meq1YkK3AHKUwMBCIVNNoV/click?signature=1ffdccf2177c9c9883d919aa125a60977af8f80e&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.nohaverhillfair.com%2F) from **3–8 pm**. Rides, food, chaos — let's do it together. **📅 Saturday, July 25th**
I'll start the morning in **Canterbury** at the [Canterbury Fair](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/Fl97sWr691Meq1YkK3AHKUwMBCIVNNoV/click?signature=ff23cce6d16c57f308e6f2638f4d4d7c5b49618c&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.canterburyfair.com%2F), then head over to **Litchfield** to celebrate [America's 250th birthday](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/Fl97sWr691Meq1YkK3AHKUwMBCIVNNoV/click?signature=380260db7a6e2a98f53e7fc0425c86cb880705a1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.litchfieldnh.gov%2FCalendar.aspx%3FEID%3D1380) 🎆! Come find me at any (or all!) of these — would love to see you there! In Solidarity, Paige [Share The Campaign](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/Fl97sWr691Meq1YkK3AHKUwMBCIVNNoV/click?signature=8fba0f8bd1ebab854d9859b972dd1bf66513b265&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.solidarity.tech%2Fahoy%2Fmessages%2FqYFskX20dqNb5cFLYkaraxpNGUi5Z6GZ%2Fclick%3Fsignature%3D61352a1c3935d6ce50513ab6e06595efd5a8d006%26url%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Flinktr.ee%252Fpaigefornh%253Futm_source%253Dig%2526utm_medium%253Dsocial%2526utm_content%253Dlink_in_bio%2526fbclid%253DPAZXh0bgNhZW0CMTEAc3J0YwZhcHBfaWQPOTM2NjE5NzQzMzkyNDU5AAGnwiKr3TdqjvWOCEA9wk4CEx5C5JBlX-tyaTPDCMiVE_4SK8pFYgHqQLIROxc_aem_YugD5GviU9KlQ3oWl1w5qQ)
