body:
Watching Abdul pour everything he has into this, knowing what's at stake for families like ours, has been one of the most humbling things I've ever witnessed.
Hi Peter,
I don't usually write these emails, but I wanted to share something with you today.
We have two weeks left in this primary, and I am in awe of my husband, Abdul. He's up before the sun and out working until long after our girls are asleep.
Believe me, he's tired, but every time I ask him why he keeps going, he tells me it's because of people like you, Peter.
Running for office asks a lot of a family. It asks even more of the person running. Watching Abdul pour everything he has into this, knowing what's at stake for families like ours, has been one of the most humbling things I've ever witnessed.
I also want you to know how grateful we are for the support. Every person who's chipped in, knocked a door, or told a friend about Abdul — you're the reason why we’re feeling this hopeful. 🙏
But two weeks is still a lot of time in the political world. These next few days are going to be extremely busy, and Abdul could use an extra bit of support.
If you’re able to, please consider pitching in to Abdul’s campaign today. Anything you can contribute goes a long way:

Inside Scoop Issue: 7/21/2026
GOP Targets Birthright Loopholes
Republicans are opening a new front against birthright citizenship after last month's Supreme Court defeat, with the [fight shifting](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckL1upjAQAJ8GOiNj8-MULq75ulx7JTL-wSsZL_IuIbmnP6W4F0g_mpHmz_v27qBAPX67M1og2gKGjTPe5GogTBWrB4a_sVLCe1NSLUKuQo2b8wwfcZtcH-ysRpNMH-24mmlZjRxln62fUwh7CMs6yyVIHbVRZom7NG_j2-xCD_bbJ1c1Kj1rLQezJD2ZuEs3jXp3vpvkfQXHcYBKECJ5xOvCAgyeBmxHX2xmvqjTvzr16tTreZ4h4WeNDw0ez069_uOdeu3QOAvGuwGdIsGRWVCGxCRuEtzwAu-KOB3HVoG_xONaEBmIsX0Jn6FGiiJ-XgWBHQPWvtlwPVAK0LJ2kzxOB-U73PNPb35Y9S8AAP__OMSL5Q) to America's five inhabited territories. Rep. Morgan Griffith argues the ruling left territorial citizenship untouched, invoking the Insular Cases as precedent. Lawmakers are also [flooding Congress](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D2unjAQheHVmM7I2Pw4hYs0dDdtSmTsASYyHuQxH1JWH5El3PJtziOd31_Ll8eEef_lT3DIvESKSz3oZp8j05YpB6z4FzJvdC9a6VGqSepu8aHiB5beN9ENurObbcB1k-3HyapONYezoVPKT3H8YUcI4O1gBgMq2G0cIvRTg-7dU5PutBmMUa0dN9NbWJXvO7P6IHp1X9FXaDEzRuBAdF2UsGLglsreJHfUerEwP4WehZ6f52kfzwfmvVKueAK3gU6h5wwPCz2_otDznzv9D6HnAte9Jgw-s9wSUZSB8l6AWa6YEr-5FcpV8n0VOEEGukuVK5Z6FNyPKvTcFBevB1NCHifRq_30mF65qd-99eP0vwAAAP__P3yMEQ) with measures aimed at birth tourism and children of temporary visa-holders. Several proposals borrow Justice Kavanaugh's statutory roadmap, pursuing [narrower fixes](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0EEOnSAQxvHT4A6DI0_twkU37l63XZoRUKZFIA4-0p6-sUkv0OVkku-f_L6_1zdSoHh8w9PNxLzaZNfi080YLac9pmio0G8XeU_3CgoGqUYJ3Yqm0MetGhs7v6Cb9qlxczdOehgn1anGz3bYhtECgur3YRy11bvZlO61c6770mFD87OnRuigf_W9aqdh7_XkNoW66zc0Qqs7WyyupchkHZuUck6BChlu03U0YfalZBb9VwGLgKXW2lZkT_EoKRY6HbcmnQKW6CoLWJ6igOXHHf4eApYjZRmwnvjTXSzzzV5GV-VGIbA0nrLEir_kRlfxFx2-yH8iz--6Hz4BS3PNNlcKgXgYhVbHiRSedlP-F_Yzw58AAAD__0bRjIg) rather than a frontal challenge to the decision. With a razor-thin House majority, passage stays uncertain, but conservatives insist codifying limits now protects the border long after Trump leaves office. ★★★
Trump Fortifies Defense Supply
President Trump signed an [executive order](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0E2OpSAUQOHV4AzDn2INGPTEWfW0hwbhqrejQLjwXqpX36kt1AbOSb4_n9unxxvT-ds_4JBoizlu7cqdfIqUj5RTwIb_INGR-6aEmrmwXMnNh4Yv2IwfopuUXI5lACftYma7CCmGy03mQ-_x8B-zDtpMfglKxn2XxgY7W60HdN89YZVUetJajMt8aLPALryReveBGdFL9A1GTIQRKORcSr6xYaAx13O43dVaIaZ_MbUytf7t1NoFCd40hvwwtZ75BTU9kBpTK0HoFdsXU2ur_SkciToQzzVC5aXmBqHxCAckAk69lPuLh8tjIu4fjByrT_zt61BdLG-8b6TZMiPOx-P9fRzaTxlfTv0PAAD__7zBiDY) Monday tightening where defense contractors may source critical minerals and sensitive components for the Pentagon's arsenal. White House trade counselor [Peter Navarro](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0LGupSAYBOCnwQ6DoMApKLaxu9tuaX7h9_gnCgTweHeffuMr3H4ymW_-fC1fQAfF92840VGtS0hhaXu6KsRQ0xZT9NToH8a6pWuRQmouDJfDAr7RB5cRuuAmOdjNdugGY0dtrBhEtzuvg3kZq_G1GiUGv05Gab3aSSkrAX1H7ukTRg5STUqJ3upNjRZXAeOgVvBsFFcO0LCnWClg9SnlnA5q5Gufyrs73N5arkz9YnJmcr7vu7-h7hTfLUX8hpMilt6nk8k54l2fzE4N-WNEJudRT5NWLybnVq4zc_xGfz00nkrAwgNuGCvyeuV8_OV-B4rcp9gK-JZK5RkbFh7hA6UkJueuuJBvOg6q2rBRvE-g41nQtZ8-_HHyfwAAAP__h1GQdQ) said the directive would close a longstanding waiver loophole that let suppliers bypass laws restricting materials from China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea. The order requires contractors to map their supply chains and disclose the origins of key metals, magnets, chips, and chemicals. Taking effect January 1, 2027, it aims to bring arms production stateside and limit reliance on adversarial nations amid mounting concerns about wartime supply shortfalls. ★★★
House Probes Bias, Fraud
House Oversight Republicans are launching a trio of [high-profile hearings](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckDGSnDAQRU8jMk2JFgPaQIETsnXqkGqkZmgXSJhuZl0-vYsr7AX-f-_9-pw-kTcur5-4U2SRKdc86VovwZKlLqWWxMr_qMhSrwkc9NYNFtoJk_Kbpg6bHJ_QhiU0FNshdP0QXOuaNfoPes756eaZwgci5L6HAQKh932bYGg43ntugBb803v3CP3iu0Czw671MybTuevIqPTgIpxJUq3HUTdWTvKo56vZ4qp6iPE_DIwGxt-XqK5U6Eseqe4GxoLKtRgYRVFJDIyJitJp5c-FJxkYb1uy9U2n8GtVS39x50J2p8wJT7LLiVe2srOuUgtjsZnY3hyJSZoz5uOLt42lH0znXjvydp83-t2i7wj_AwAA__-q8Ywy) this week on longstanding conservative priorities. A health subcommittee roundtable will examine Medicare fraud tied to skin-substitute spending, building on revelations of roughly nine billion dollars in Minnesota benefits fraud. Separately, the committee is [scrutinizing the Smithsonian](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D-O6yAQgPHTQBeLGTCQguI17vLaLS3Cn2Qkh7ECiVd7-lWusAf4vuL3dVkvkTZqt__xUQL1vmbO67jzq8eWO9fGLdGgn9J65deKCu1JuRPCGtOgd1lNlDnMCL56WQI4b6zzCpS8B-3mpEpNFet51mdnSvGz1_ZqzwAelKTw-SmHgHrWWk3eVm18uapoQF9jEka99hxHmah1yqUn5n3njQalPvHzJrdwH2PvQv8TuAhcjuOYKn-3cvQp8UPg8qZcWOBijQKH3hoAQPkMeT9o26hbJ4y6PSJtn0COvyq8A_4GAAD__0trbAk) after a White House report accused the National Museum of American History of distorting and disparaging the nation's past. A third session targets diversity, equity, and inclusion policies that Trump's early executive orders sought to dismantle. Members frame the probes as accountability for institutions they say drifted sharply leftward under prior leadership.
Midterm Battlefield Tightens

Cost of living has vaulted to the top of voter concerns, and Fox's latest [power rankings](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckLsOnDAQRb8GOiM_eLhxkYZu06ZEw9jAKOBBjHfZzddHW-QHUt-rc6Tz6zE9gHbK6084UiCRKXKcysZPgRyFl8wZqdCflGXh52S17ZUelDUTYKFXmlqoY-is8YuvUzCDb_vBa6PrLaTOxejmiHPXtQt4g9EjzhotWkDT1RS-PD1YY13nnG58v7jWp1lDa9wMWLX6eUYoqaEsFJMg83nyToVQGr7Weg9bKadU7kdlx8qO9303C79zuqVBPio7_rtXdlz4rb6LOvlOl7og_6a8inpxSZcogY8qW_pcSSXkzAehOoGyiulgvKCIWoFyfYV43rTvJP1QtXo9gPavrC7_W_AV7N8AAAD__0w_h3A) show Democrats gaining ground as lingering economic pain threatens to overshadow the structural advantages Republicans carry into November's high-stakes contests.

★★★
Speaker's Fundraising Juggernaut

Speaker Mike Johnson posted a $19.1 million second quarter, pushing his cycle total past $135 million, and is already [redirecting cash](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckEGSpCAQAF-DNw0saWQPHPbirfe6RwOh0JrBwhBsJ-b1E_2F-UBmZP5_zk9HiXj953a0VMoccpjrlq_iOJQcObOnSt_IJeZrBgm6lWML_ex8pRfOyjXBPqA30TRo-9EoPRrZy2azHhfzRwctfUATfVSL1Bj8YAxEUMvYkH3z5Ag9DI9hkJ3RcVAGF-lUPyzOCyWvI7iKHXGhgMXnfBw5USVfunyuTbJbrUcRw18Bk4Dpvu_udmUjXmtm_HI7MZ6dz7uAifEuAqZ3HQqYlFbGgBIw7fSJ7UfeuGRuX1diPN2SsD3xuJZE3nFp48XhdFSI13ZzVxIwNacNx00pUdGjUHLdHaW3q6m_ffmy8BMAAP__acKI7w) to vulnerable Republicans tasked with defending the party's narrow House majority this fall.

★★★
GOP Holds Cash Edge

That's not a hypothetical. It's happening.
In a single year, nearly 2,500 active research grants at the NIH were canceled. Another 2,000 at the National Science Foundation. Over $5 billion in already-approved medical and scientific research -- wiped out without warning. Cancer centers. Early-career scientists. Clinical trials already underway. Gone.
Here's what makes it worse: Congress had already approved that money. It was law. And it still got clawed back while the people we sent to Washington looked the other way.
In 1964, America invested nearly two cents of every federal dollar into scientific research. That commitment gave us disease eradication, the Moon landing, the internet -- and decades of economic growth and longer, healthier lives. Every dollar invested returned more than two dollars in economic activity.
Today? We're spending less than seven-tenths of one cent on the dollar. We didn't lose our ambition. Congress stopped supporting it.
Every cure your family has ever benefited from started as a publicly funded discovery. Every high-tech industry powering our economy -- biotech, healthcare, medical devices, half of Seattle's economy -- grew out of research America used to fund without blinking.
What happens when that stops?
I'm Melissa Chaudhry, and I'm running for Congress in Washington's 9th District because this isn't an academic problem. It's yours. It's mine.
Here's what I'll fight for:
✅ Restore and sustain high-level federal investment in science and research
✅ Rebuild America's leading edge in innovation and technology
✅ Real congressional oversight -- so authorized research funding can't quietly disappear again
I'm doing it taking zero corporate PAC money. No foreign interests. No defense contractors. No health insurance companies. The only people I answer to are the ones this research is supposed to save.
**Care. Courage. The Constitution.**
